title: Civil Defence Shelter and Fire Safety (Miscellaneous Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Civil Defence Shelter and Fire Safety (Miscellaneous Amendment) Bill

sections.label: SCDF fire safety amendments
sections.summary: Four changes: strengthen SCDF oversight of shelter products, class licensing for P&FM, appoint SEOs, and clarify fire safety responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: One, to strengthen SCDF's oversight over regulated shelter products and empower SCDF to take appropriate actions against parties in the supply chain for non-compliance; two, to introduce a class licensing regime for the regulation of P&FM activities; three, to allow SCDF to appoint SEOs to conduct compliance checks for the transport of P&FM; and four, to clarify the responsibilities of premise owners and occupiers in relation to fire safety measures.

sections.label: SCDF enforcement against non-compliant shelter parties
sections.summary: The amendments close a gap and give SCDF enforcement powers against errant laboratories, suppliers and installers of non-compliant shelter products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The amendments will close this gap and give SCDF enforcement powers against errant laboratories, suppliers and installers of non-compliant shelter products.

sections.label: Fire-rated door label misuse case
sections.summary: In December 2018, a COC holder gave 50 labels to a non-certified company for non-compliant doors installed in various buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In December 2018, a COC holder for fire-rated doors had utilised its certification status and provided a non-certified company with 50 labels to be pasted on non-compliant doors that were then installed in various buildings.

sections.label: New shelter supply chain offences
sections.summary: New offences cover laboratories issuing false reports, false information for COC, certifying bodies, suppliers and installers of non-compliant shelter products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, there are new offences covering parties across the shelter products supply chain who may compromise public safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These offences cover: one, accredited laboratories that issue false test reports; two, persons who provide false information to accredited certification bodies to obtain COC; three, certification bodies that certify non-compliant shelter products; four, suppliers who pass off non-compliant products as certified ones; and five, installers who fit non-compliant products or install them in a way that undermines the shelter's ability to function safely.

sections.label: Number of shelter product entities
sections.summary: The number of entities supplying shelter products is relatively small, with only five approved shelter door suppliers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Today, the number of entities involved in supply of shelter products is relatively small, for example there are only five approved shelter door suppliers.

sections.label: Appeal mechanism and composition sum
sections.summary: An appeal mechanism to the Minister for Home Affairs will be introduced, and the maximum composition sum raised from $500 to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We will introduce an appeal mechanism to the Minister for Home Affairs for parties aggrieved by SCDF's directions under the new Part 2A in relation to regulated shelter products.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We will also raise the maximum composition sum from $500 to $5,000.

sections.label: SCDF P&FM licences issued annually
sections.summary: SCDF issues more than 6,500 individual licences annually for storage, transport and conveyance of P&FM in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Today, SCDF issues more than 6,500 individual licences annually for the storage, transport and conveyance of P&FM in Singapore.

sections.label: Four lower-risk premises categories covered
sections.summary: It covers petrol stations, construction sites, Category C and D laboratories, and buildings storing diesel for emergency generators, about 15% of P&FM storage licensees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It will cover four categories of lower-risk premises: one, petrol stations; two, construction sites; three, Category C and D laboratories as specified in the Singapore Standards, which are laboratories assessed to be of low and minimal fire hazard risk respectively; and four, buildings which store diesel solely to fuel their emergency generators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These four categories account for approximately 15% of all P&FM storage licensees.

sections.label: Clause 24 powers over P&FM vehicles
sections.summary: Clause 24 clarifies powers to stop, inspect and sample P&FM vehicles, and empowers SCDF to direct vehicles along approved routes for safe disposal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Apart from clarifying existing powers such as stopping and inspecting vehicles transporting P&FM, and taking samples of the P&FM for testing, clause 24 will also empower SCDF to direct a vehicle to be driven along approved routes to a suitable location for the safe disposal of the transported P&FM.

sections.label: Clause 6 fire hazard obstruction
sections.summary: Clause 6 makes clear that a fire hazard includes obstruction of fire safety measures outside a building such as fire engine access roads and accessways.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 6 therefore makes clear that a fire hazard includes the obstruction of fire safety measures outside of a building such as fire engine access roads and accessways.

sections.label: Clause 26 licence duration increase
sections.summary: Clause 26 increases the maximum duration of any licence or permit under Part 6 of the Fire Safety Act from three years to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In line with the whole-of-Government pro-enterprise efforts to reduce regulatory burden on businesses, clause 26 increases the maximum duration of any licence or permit issued under Part 6 of the Fire Safety Act from three years to five years.

sections.label: NEA and SCDF scheduled chemicals mandate
sections.summary: NEA and SCDF already regulated hazardous substances and P&FM transport, so both agencies' mandates were expanded to cover scheduled chemicals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As the National Environment Agency (NEA) and SCDF were already regulating the transportation of hazardous substances and P&FM respectively, it made sense to expand both agencies' mandates to also cover scheduled chemicals.

sections.label: Repeal of CWPAA
sections.summary: The CWPAA is being repealed after streamlined arrangements for transporting scheduled chemicals worked well since 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: With these changes, persons transporting scheduled chemicals have benefited from the streamlined arrangement as they are only required to either apply to NEA or SCDF, depending on the type of chemical being transported.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: With processes working well since 2023, we are hereby repealing the CWPAA.

sections.label: Fire incidents and SCDF calls
sections.summary: News reports of fire incidents are borne out by data showing SCDF responded to over 2,000 fire calls in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: At the same time, there have been a series of news reports this year about various fire incidents in our Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats, commercial shops and industrial buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This is borne out in data too – the SCDF responded to more than 2,000 fire calls in 2025, which is a 10% increase compared to 2021.

sections.label: Residential fire incidence decrease
sections.summary: Residential fire incidence decreased slightly from 0.067% in 2021 to 0.065% in 2025 despite increased housing stock.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Senior Minister, Coordinating Minister for National Security and the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The incidence of residential fires has also decreased slightly, from 0.067% in 2021 to 0.065% in 2025, even as our housing stock has actually increased over the same period.

sections.label: Criteria for class licence
sections.summary: The question asks the Ministry to clarify the criteria companies must meet to operate under a class licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry provide greater clarity then, on the criteria that companies must meet before they can operate under a class licence?

sections.label: Audit regime and risk indicators
sections.summary: The question asks whether the audit regime will be purely periodic or also respond to risk indicators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the audit regime be purely periodic, or will it also respond dynamically to risk indicators such as previous breaches, changes in operations, incident reports, or significant turnover of safety personnel?

sections.label: SCDF piloting automation technologies
sections.summary: The question asks whether SCDF is piloting such technologies and has identified processes where automation would benefit most.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share whether SCDF is already currently piloting such technologies and whether it has identified particular inspection or compliance processes where automation would deliver the greatest benefit?

sections.label: Safety audits for older facilities
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government intends to mandate periodic safety audits and lifecycle maintenance for facilities crossing 30 or 40 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such facilities across Singapore cross the 30- or 40-year mark, does the Government intend to mandate periodic safety audits and proactive lifecycle maintenance to mitigate long-term structural and fire safety risks?

sections.label: Class licence criteria and audits
sections.summary: Asks MHA for details on class licence criteria, SCDF assessment of safety systems and officers, and audit scope and frequency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) provide further details on the criteria that companies must meet before commencing operations under the respective class licences?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, how will the SCDF assess a company’s safety systems, past compliance record, the professional competence of its responsible officers and its ability to manage P&FMs safely?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Minister also provide more details on the expected scope and frequency of post-licensing audits?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the audit regime be periodic or will the audit frequency be adjusted dynamically according to risk indicators, such as previous breaches, changes in business operations, incident reports or significant changes in safety personnel?

sections.label: Five deaths in HDB fires
sections.summary: States that five residents died following separate fires in HDB flats between 28 July and 1 September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Just recently, between 28 July and 1 September, five residents died following separate fires in HDB flats.

sections.label: Exit door locks in residential units
sections.summary: Asks whether new section 27A(v) on obstructions applies to a residential entrance gate with a double cylinder lock or padlock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The present Fire Code generally requires exit doors to be openable from the inside without a key, a tool or special knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, residential units remain exempt from that requirement and it does not seem that the Bill changes this position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I ask the Senior Minister of State if they could clarify If the new section 27A(v) of the Fire Safety Act on obstructions would therefore apply to a residential entrance gate with a double cylinder keyed lock or a padlock that forms the only practical route out of a unit.

sections.label: HIP upgrade to thumb turn gates
sections.summary: Asks whether MHA or the Ministry for National Development considered a January proposal to use HIP to upgrade older flats to gates with interior thumb turns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State update the House on whether MHA or his colleagues in the Ministry for National Development have considered my January proposal to use the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) as a means to upgrade older flats to gates with an interior thumb turn?

sections.label: Rise in fire injuries and fatalities
sections.summary: States fire injuries rose from 80 in 2024 to 94 in 2025 and fatalities from five to six, with five deaths from 31 July to 1 September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Fire injuries rose from 80 in 2024 to 94 in 2025, and fire fatalities from five to six over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More alarming still, in the short span from 31 July to 1 September this year alone, five lives have already been lost to fire incidents.

sections.label: Dry risers failing after servicing
sections.summary: SCDF reported dry rises failed in recent fires despite maintenance records showing they were serviced and pressure tested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The House will recall that, in several recent fires, SCDF reported that it could not get the dry rises to work and that its, officers were forced to carry hoses up the stairs to fight the fire by hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This was especially unfortunate because the maintenance records indicated that those very rises had been serviced and pressure tested and were found to be in order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That gap between a record that says serviced and a riser that fails at the moment of truth is exactly where lives can be lost.

sections.label: Fire Safety Act amendments questions
sections.summary: The Member asks about critical danger grounds, chemical amendments, dry riser failures, infrastructure checks and corridor obstruction accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Section 4K allows this on the grounds of “critical danger”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, on the amendments to the Fire Safety Act, regarding chemicals, I would like the Minister to elaborate on what is new in this Bill, beyond simply consolidating the existing legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On cases involving fire, there have also been recent incidents where dry riser systems failed to function even though they had only recently been serviced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, how will the Government ensure that infrastructure, such as dry riser systems mentioned earlier, is in working order?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And where common corridors are obstructed by residents’ belongings, should the residents or the Town Council be accountable?

sections.label: SCDF powers over shelter products
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens SCDF's powers over regulated shelter products, including testing, certification, and directing recall, removal or rectification of non-compliant products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens SCDF's powers over regulated shelter products, including testing and certification, and the ability to direct non-compliant products to be recalled, removed or rectified.

sections.label: Obstruction and interference provisions
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens provisions dealing with obstruction of access roads and accessways and interference with fire safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens provisions dealing with the obstruction of access roads and accessways and interference with fire safety measures.

sections.label: Compliance checks for P&FM transport
sections.summary: The Bill expands their role to conduct compliance checks relating to the transport of P&FM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Bill expands their role to conduct compliance checks relating to the transport of P&FM.

sections.label: Powers to stop and inspect
sections.summary: The powers include stopping and inspecting vehicles, checking documents, taking samples and directing a vehicle elsewhere for safe unloading or disposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The powers include stopping and inspecting vehicles, checking documents, taking samples and where necessary directing a vehicle elsewhere for safe unloading or disposal.

sections.label: SCDF operational experience feedback
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SCDF feeds inspection learning back into the organisation and that officers build operational experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today's routine inspection may provide the experience needed to handle tomorrow's complex incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, as SEOs take on more of this work, I hope SCDF will ensure that what we see and learn is fed back into the organisation and that our SCDF officers continue to build operational experience themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need strong rules where public safety is at stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But those rules also need to work in practice.

sections.label: Stronger powers, better safety
sections.summary: Stronger powers must ultimately translate into better safety on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Ultimately, stronger powers must translate into better safety on the ground.

sections.label: Extending licence and permit validity
sections.summary: The Bill extends the maximum validity period of licences and permits under the Fire Safety Act from three to five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The other significant change in the Bill is to extend the maximum validity period of licenses and permits issued under the Fire Safety Act from three years to five years.

sections.label: Clause 26 validity extension
sections.summary: Clause 26 extends licence or permit validity under the Fire Safety Act from three to five years to reduce compliance costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 26 of the Bill proposes to extend the validity period of licences or permits issued under the Fire Safety Act from three years to five years to reduce compliance costs for businesses.

sections.label: Question on fire safety risk
sections.summary: The question asks whether extending licence and permit validity from three to five years increases fire safety risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the extension of the validity period of licenses and permits from three to five years, is the fire safety risk increased?

sections.label: May fire in ward
sections.summary: A fire in May guttered a coffee shop and had distressing ramifications for residents living above it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Residents in my ward experienced this first-hand in May this year when a fire not only guttered the coffee shop itself but had distressing ramifications for residents living above it.

sections.label: Fire safety knowledge of food staff
sections.summary: The passage asks how many food establishment personnel know how to contain a fire, operate gas shut-off valves and use fire extinguishers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If a fire were to happen, how many of the personnel at the food establishments would know how to contain it?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How many know that there are emergency shut-off valves, or snap valves to cut off gas supply and are trained to operate it?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Do they know how to use fire extinguishers?

sections.label: Fire safety as non-negotiable priority
sections.summary: The passage states that easing compliance burden on businesses must not weaken commitment to fire safety as a non-negotiable priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even as this Bill seeks to ease the compliance burden on businesses, we must never lose our commitment to fire safety as a non-negotiable priority.

sections.label: Strict liability and shelter certification
sections.summary: The passage states that strict liability for obstructing fire access ways and fire safety measures brings clarity, and mandatory certification and accredited laboratory testing elevate shelter product standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The establishment of strict liability for obstructing fire access ways and fire safety measures brings much needed clarity to statutory compliance, elevating standards for shelter products through mandatory certification and accredited laboratory testing ensures that emergency shelters retain their protected integrity when residents need them most.

sections.label: SCDF notices to Town Councils
sections.summary: The passage describes SCDF notifying Town Councils of fire safety concerns in HDB flats and serving Fire Hazard Abatement Notices if issues remain past a three-day window.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, when a fire safety concern in an HDB flat is flagged, SCDF typically notifies the Town Council about the specific unit involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, under section 28 of the Fire Safety Act, if an issue remains outstanding past SCDF's strict three-day action window, sometimes due to practical ground difficulties, such as uncooperative residents or individuals who briefly remove clutter only to replace days later, SCDF may serve a formal Fire Hazard Abatement Notice to the Town Council.

sections.label: Offence for obstructing escape routes
sections.summary: The passage states that clause 12 replaces section 27 of the Fire Safety Act to make obstructing an escape route or common property an explicit statutory offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 12 replaces section 27 of the Fire Safety Act to make it an explicit statutory offence for any person to cause an obstruction to an escape route, or common property that renders escape in the event of a fire more difficult.

sections.label: Notice specifying offending unit numbers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice to a Town Council can specify exact offending unit numbers instead of citing the entire block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, when SCDF issues an Fire Hazard Abatement Notice to a Town Council, can the notice specify the exact offending unit numbers rather than broadly citing the entire block which obliges Town Councils to execute blanket enforcement operations across the whole block?

sections.label: SCDF fire calls and casualties
sections.summary: In 2025, SCDF responded to 2,050 fire calls, over half in residential premises, with 94 hospital-admission injuries and six fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, SCDF responded to 2,050 fire calls, more than half, or 1,051 of these calls were fires in residential premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: There were 94 injuries requiring hospital admissions and six fatalities.

sections.label: Older shelter door serviceability
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether there is a proportionate way to ensure older shelter doors remain serviceable over their lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: That particular door may have deteriorated because of age, rust or wear and tear.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, my first question to the Senior Minister of State is do we have a proportionate way of making sure that this older shelter product remains serviceable over an entire lifespan?

sections.label: Common corridor escape passage advice
sections.summary: SCDF advises residential common corridors retain at least 1.2 metres of unobstructed escape passages.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: SCDF currently advises that in residential common corridor should retain at least 1.2 metres of unobstructed escape passages.

sections.label: SCDF fire safety enforcement checks
sections.summary: In 2025, SCDF conducted 14,750 fire safety enforcement checks, issuing 2,668 abatement notices and 1,209 notices of offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2025, SCDF conducted 14,750 fire safety enforcement checks, issuing 2,668 fire hazard abatement notices and 1,209 notice of offences.

sections.label: Class licensing for lower-risk activities
sections.summary: The speaker supports reducing regulatory burden for lower-risk activities and notes MHA identified four class licensing categories with no fires from 2020 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I support reducing unnecessary regulatory burden for activities that genuinely shows lower risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand for a start that MHA has identified four categories of activities for class licensing.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As mentioned, there were no fires reported involving these categories between 2020 and 2025 earlier.

sections.label: Class licensing approval process change
sections.summary: Under class licensing, eligible premises will no longer undergo the same periodic individual licence approval or renewal process with SCDF.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: With class licensing, eligible premises will no longer go through the same periodic individual licence approval or renewal process with SCDF.

sections.label: Class licence review triggers
sections.summary: The MP asks what would trigger SCDF review, variation or revocation of a class licence, and whether lighter regulation preserves safety outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, will SCDF monitor inspection findings, rates of non-compliance, near misses or actual incidents across each case, and are there thresholds or indicators that would prompt SCDF to review whether a particular class of licence should continue unchanged?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill provides the ability to vary and revoke a class licence, as well as disapply to a particular operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State share what would trigger these actions?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Reducing unnecessary administrative burdens makes sense, but lighter touch regulation must give us the same confidence as the underlying safety outcomes.

sections.label: Civil Defence Shelter Act amendment
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Civil Defence Shelter Act and grants the Commissioner of Civil Defence enhanced powers for regulatory oversight over shelter products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One significant effect of the current Bill is to amend the Civil Defence Shelter Act and grant the Commissioner of civil defence with enhanced powers so that SCDF can better exercise its regulatory oversight over shelter products.

sections.label: Section 4H direction grounds
sections.summary: The Commissioner can issue a section 4H direction on reasonable grounds of public safety necessity and non-compliant or impairing shelter products, covering an enforcement gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Bill, the Commissioner can issue a section 4H direction if he or she has reasonable grounds to believe that (a) the direction is necessary for public safety; and (b) the shelter product is either non-compliant or was installed in a manner that impairs or is likely to impair the safe and efficient use of the shelter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the Senior Minister of State explained, the new section 4H directions cover an existing enforcement gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I also note that a 4 August 2026 CNA report stated that SCDF has not identified any cases of non-compliant shelter products.

sections.label: Power-driven nails in shelters
sections.summary: The MP asks SCDF to confirm whether wall-mounted air-conditioners or fans fixed with power-driven nails on household shelter internal walls are prohibited in HDB and non-HDB shelters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, can SCDF also confirm that the installation of a wall-mounted air-conditioning, or a wall-mounted fan would be prohibited if they are fixed using power-driven nails onto the internal walls of the household shelter, and that this applies to both HDB and non-HDB household shelters?

sections.label: Toa Payoh fire 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, a major fire broke out at a residential block along Lorong 8 Toa Payoh in the MP's constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2025, a major fire broke out at a residential block along Lorong 8 Toa Payoh in my constituency.

sections.label: Fire-engine access obstruction provisions
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens provisions on obstruction of fire-engine access roads and accessways, and on interference with fire-safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill strengthens the provisions dealing with obstruction of fire-engine access roads and accessways, as well as interference with fire-safety measures.

sections.label: Smart sensors for fire-safety equipment
sections.summary: Asks whether SCDF and agencies could explore wider use of smart sensors and IoT to monitor critical fire-safety equipment in high-rise residential buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For high-rise residential buildings in particular, could SCDF, together with HDB, Town Councils and the relevant agencies, explore the wider use of smart sensors, Internet-of-Things monitoring and other technologies to continuously monitor the operational status of critical fire-safety equipment?

sections.label: Testing and replacing ageing fire-safety equipment
sections.summary: Asks whether older critical fire-safety equipment should face more regular testing and clearer triggers for accelerated replacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Relatedly, could we consider whether older critical fire-safety equipment should be subject to more regular operational testing or drills as it ages, and whether there should be clearer triggers for accelerated replacement where equipment repeatedly develops faults or is approaching the end of its reliable service life?

sections.label: Pilots for critical fire-safety systems
sections.summary: Suggests SCDF consider pilots with HDB and Town Councils in older or higher-risk buildings, assessing costs, reliability and safety benefits before wider deployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Not every piece of equipment needs a sensor and the economics may not make sense everywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But for critical systems where failure could have serious consequences, SCDF could consider pilots with HDB and Town Councils, particularly in older or higher-risk buildings, and assess the costs, reliability and actual safety benefits before wider deployment.

sections.label: Regulated shelter products framework
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a regulatory framework for regulated shelter products used in household and storey shelters, subject to standards and certification including COCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a regulatory framework for "regulated shelter products" used in household and storey shelters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These products will be subject to applicable standards and certification requirements, including COCs.

sections.label: Supporting new market entrants
sections.summary: Asks how SCDF will ensure new entrants to the approved supplier list are supported to meet required standards from the outset.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Senior Minister of State mentioned that SCDF had previously consulted the industry in 2024 on these changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I would also like to ask the Senior Minister of State to consider: first, as the regulatory framework matures and the approved supplier list potentially expands, how would SCDF ensure that new entrants to the market are adequately supported to meet the required standards from the outset, rather than discovering gaps only after a product has been supplied or installed?

sections.label: Imminent danger threshold safeguards
sections.summary: Asks how the threshold of imminent danger affecting public safety will be applied and what safeguards and internal authorisations govern such powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State therefore elaborate on how the threshold of "imminent danger affecting public safety" will be applied in practice and what safeguards and internal authorisations will govern the use of such powers?

sections.label: Class licensing risk criteria
sections.summary: Asks what risk criteria determine suitability for class licensing and how SCDF will monitor compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State share what risk criteria will determine whether an activity is suitable for class licensing and how SCDF will continue to monitor compliance?

sections.label: Operational coordination with other agencies
sections.summary: Asks how interventions will be coordinated operationally with other agencies when vehicles are stopped, diverted or escorted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Senior Minister of State elaborate on how such interventions will be coordinated operationally with other agencies, where necessary, particularly where a vehicle has to be stopped, diverted or escorted on a busy road?

sections.label: Member supports the Bill
sections.summary: The Member states that with these clarifications, he supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With these clarifications, Sir, I support the Bill.

sections.label: SCDF regulates shelter doors only
sections.summary: SCDF will for now regulate only shelter doors as a critical component of shelter structural integrity and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: For now, SCDF will regulate only shelter doors as they are a critical component to structural integrity and effectiveness of the shelter.

sections.label: Costs of defective shelter products
sections.summary: SCDF directs the responsible party in the supply chain to bear costs of testing and rectification of defective shelter products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Third, on who will bear the cost of inspection or replacement of a defective shelter product if the home owner had bought the flat in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: It is also the same principle that guides SCDF's approach, which is to direct the responsible party in the supply chain, whether the certification body, supplier, installer or building owner, to bear the costs of testing and rectification.

sections.label: Statutory protection for innocent home owners
sections.summary: The Bill provides statutory protection for innocent home owners under the new section 4F.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The Bill also provides important statutory protection for innocent home owners under the new section 4F.

sections.label: No non-compliant products found
sections.summary: Members are reminded that no cases of non-compliant products have been encountered to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In fact, I would also like to remind Members that we have not come across any cases of non-compliant products to date.

sections.label: SCDF notice and warrant
sections.summary: SCDF will give at least 24 hours' notice or obtain a Magistrate's warrant, with a high threshold of real immediate risk of harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Wherever possible, SCDF will give the owner or occupier at least 24 hours' notice, or obtain a Magistrate's warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The threshold will be very high such as where there is a real immediate risk of harm to persons.

sections.label: SCDF risk study and compliance
sections.summary: SCDF studied the risks and found no reported fires from P&FM storage at these premises between 2020 and 2025, with only two administrative non-compliance cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, SCDF has studied the risks professionally, and satisfied itself that this is a safe move as there have not been any reported fires originating from P&FM storage at these premises between 2020 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In fact, the extent of regulatory compliance in these four categories is strong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: There were only two cases of non-compliance from the more than 500 premises in these four categories, and the two cases were due to administrative oversight – paperwork.

sections.label: Estimated savings for eligible premises
sections.summary: Eligible premises can expect to save about $300,000 in licensing fees and 330 man-hours annually through one-time registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Based on SCDF's estimates, eligible premises can collectively expect to save approximately $300,000 in licensing fees annually as well as about 330 man-hours annually through the one-time registration process and removal of recurring licence renewal requirements.

sections.label: Reduced licence validity after revocation
sections.summary: Where a licence is revoked for non-compliance, SCDF will reduce the validity of the next licence to one year for two licensing cycles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Where a licence has been revoked due to non-compliance, SCDF will reduce the validity of any subsequent licence issued to the same business to one year for the next two licensing cycles.

sections.label: SEO scope and Town Councils
sections.summary: Removal of items from common areas is under Town Councils and not within the SEO's responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Mr Giam had requested to widen the SEO's scope so they can be deployed to engage persistent non-compliant units directly rather than relying on Town Council for item removals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I want to stress that the removal of items from common areas is under the ambit of Town Councils and this is not within the scope of the SEO's responsibilities.

sections.label: Fire safety measures kept unobstructed
sections.summary: Clauses 6, 10, 11 and 12 aim to make clear that fire safety measures outside or on the building exterior must be kept unobstructed and in working order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: One of the main objectives of clauses 6, 10, 11 and 12 is to make clear that fire safety measures which are located outside the building or on the exterior of the building must be kept unobstructed and in working order.

sections.label: SCDF graduated enforcement approach
sections.summary: SCDF uses a calibrated approach: Abatement Notices for minor non-compliance, composition fines for more severe or repeated breaches, and prosecution for egregious breaches or failure to rectify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: SCDF already adopts a calibrated and graduated approach to enforcement against fire safety breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Abatement Notices are generally issued for minor cases of non-compliance, while composition fines may be imposed for more severe non-compliances or repeated breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Prosecution may be considered for egregious breaches or where the responsible party fails to rectify the fire safety non-compliances.

sections.label: AI-driven inspection tool
sections.summary: SCDF and the Home Team Science and Technology Agency developed the Targeted On-Site Inspection Tool, an AI-driven predictive model that scores premises for likelihood of fire safety violations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: For example, SCDF, and Home Team Science and Technology Agency have developed the Targeted On-Site Inspection Tool, which uses an AI-driven predictive model that draws data from various sources, such as building information, inspection and enforcement records to identify premises with a higher likelihood of fire safety violations, and generates a score for each premises.

sections.label: Retroactive upgrades for older blocks
sections.summary: Where necessary, the Government has required retroactive upgrades to older blocks with critical requirements such as dry risers and exit staircases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Where necessary, the Government has required retroactive upgrades to older blocks with critical requirements, such as dry risers and exit staircases.

sections.label: Stringent licensing for higher risk premises
sections.summary: Higher risk premises such as oil refineries must meet more stringent licensing requirements, including regular audits, inspections and testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: For example, higher risk premises, such as oil refineries are required to meet more stringent licensing requirements, which includes regular audits, inspections and testing requirements.

sections.label: HIP lock options
sections.summary: Under the HIP, there are two options: a double-cylinder lock and a thumb-turn lock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Under the HIP, there are two options – a double-cylinder lock and a thumb-turn lock.

sections.label: Fire safety amendments for businesses
sections.summary: The amendments clarify roles and obligations, empower SCDF against errant suppliers, free enforcement resources, and keep regulatory burden reasonable while maintaining fire safety standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: This is what these amendments today seek to reinforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: It provides: (a) better clarity on roles and obligations of businesses, business owners, occupiers and residents, so that they can be more aware of how they contribute to fire safety; (b) this empowers SCDF to take errant suppliers, certification bodies and testing labs to task when violations occur; (c) it frees up scarce enforcement resources so SCDF can focus on more complex issues, such as investigating possible P&FM offences; and (d) ensures that the overall regulatory burden on businesses remains reasonable, by reducing administrative burden where possible, while maintaining high fire safety standards.
